name: EditorConfig Inspector
description: Explain which .editorconfig rules apply to a file: matching sections, each property's value and source line, and what was overridden or unset
help: Follows EditorConfig specification 0.17: .editorconfig files are read from the file's directory upwards until one has root = true; nearer files win, later sections in a file win, and unset removes an inherited property.

Globs support * / ** / ? / [abc] / [!abc] / {a,b} (nestable) / {1..10} numeric ranges and \ escapes. A glob without / matches file names at any depth; one with / is relative to the config's directory.

Specification-defined derivations are marked separately: indent_style = tab without indent_size gives indent_size = tab, and a numeric indent_size without tab_width sets tab_width. Standard properties that are not set show “not set” instead of any editor's default.

Invalid values of standard properties are kept verbatim and flagged; max_line_length and editor-specific extensions are listed as extensions, not errors. Target files may not exist yet; only the path matters.

Only configuration inside the chosen project folder is read, never above it; if no root = true is found by the project root, the result is marked as possibly incomplete. You can also paste a single configuration to use as the project root's file. The tool is read-only and never changes configuration or source files.

result.invalidHint: Not a value allowed by the specification; editors may ignore it
